issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This epic tracks the attempt to make Grug's local MoE expert MLP path fast by adapting SonicMoE ideas into a JAX-callable Marin backend. The investigation narrowed from broad Sonic/QuACK custom-call options to the local grouped `w13` / activation / grouped `w2` path and gather/combine behavior on GH200/H200-class GPUs. By mid-May 2026, plain JAX/Pallas paths had shown useful forward performance but not enough backward/remat improvement; the production-facing direction then narrowed to PR #5718's `implementation="sonic"` backend, which keeps existing JAX `ragged_dot` grouped GEMMs and ports Sonic's token gather/combine kernel through `jax-triton` with a custom VJP. The remaining work is to validate that backend in realistic GPU training shapes and keep the more fragile CuTe/QuACK ragged-TMA experiments as research notes, not default production dependencies.

### Helpful links
- Latest production-path update: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4484868494
- PR #5718 scope update: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4484780037
- jax-triton train-step comparison: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4449166706
- CuTe/QuACK ragged-TMA reproducer result: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4453791007
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Goal

Produce and land a local MoE kernel backend for GH200/H200-class NVIDIA GPUs that materially improves Grug's local expert MLP path on the authoritative GPU benchmark cells, with a clear interface boundary against the transport layer.

Success target for this research thread: find a JAX-callable path, or a custom-call path usable from JAX, that gets within roughly 10-20% of Sonic/QuACK on the local MoE block.

## Scope

In scope:
- local grouped `w13` / activation / grouped `w2` path
- local gather-and-sum / combine behavior
- activation-memory-efficient local backward bookkeeping where it matters
- Pallas, Mosaic GPU, custom-call, or direct Sonic/QuACK wrapper routes that can be called from JAX
- comparisons against `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py`

Out of scope:
- DeepEP-equivalent dispatch/return transport
- ring vs `ragged_all_to_all` transport design
- broad PyTorch interop layers unrelated to a measured local-kernel win
- router/top-k redesign unless a local kernel requires a narrowly scoped metadata change

## Current Baseline

Primary GH200 shape: `tokens=8192`, `hidden=2048`, `intermediate=3072`, `experts=8`, `topk=2`, BF16.

| Measure | Real Sonic/QuACK | Best JAX/Grug path so far | Gap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| forward | `1.260ms` | `1.285ms` | `+2.0%` |
| `fwd_bwd` | `3.428ms` | `4.035ms` | `+17.7%` |
| `fwd2_bwd` proxy | `4.428ms` | `5.640ms` | `+27.4%` |
| `remat_bwd` / checkpoint | `4.798ms` | `5.844ms` with `prevent_cse=True` | `+21.8%` |

Interpretation:
- Use `fwd_bwd` for ordinary no-remat training comparisons.
- Use `remat_bwd` with `prevent_cse=True` for honest forced-recompute comparisons.
- Do not use the older JAX `remat_bwd=4.056ms` number for parity claims; that used `prevent_cse=False` and appears to have benefited from XLA CSE/reuse across the checkpoint boundary.

## Latest Update

Latest issue comment: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4484868494

Latest local logbook entries:
- `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-jax-triton-overhead.md`: raw Sonic jax-triton gather/combine train-step probes
- `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-pallas-grug.md`, `SONIC-PALLAS-044`: CuTe DSL JAX integration smoke and follow-up ragged-TMA blockers

Local handoff: `/Users/dlwh/src/marin/scratch/moe-block-decomposition-handoff-20260513.md`

## Decision Log

- 2026-04-30: narrowed the broad SonicMoE scout to this local-compute epic for Grug MoE GMM/MLP.
- 2026-05-10: Pallas unpack-backward VJP produced a small real training win, about `2.8%` end-to-end on the 006a-style 1x GH200 synthetic run.
- 2026-05-11: full forward path is close enough to Sonic; the remaining question moved to full-block backward and remat behavior.
- 2026-05-12: direct Mosaic GPU vector-indexed metadata/gather path hit JAX lowering blockers; scalar Mosaic workaround lowered but did not close the Sonic gap.
- 2026-05-13: full-block comparison shows best JAX no-remat path is `+17.7%` vs Sonic, but honest remat is `+21.8%` vs Sonic.
- 2026-05-13: naive activation+W13 Pallas/Triton fusion was rejected. It avoids materializing `d_w13_out` but recomputes the SwiGLU derivative across many matmul tiles and runs at `29.361ms` vs `1.836ms` for the materialized baseline.
- 2026-05-13: pure JAX whole-local-MoE `custom_vjp` scaffold was rejected as a speed path. It is locally correct and useful as an ABI scaffold, but full-shape GH200 timing was `12.804ms fwd_bwd` and `14.430ms remat_bwd`, far slower than `sonic_xla`.
- 2026-05-13: Sonic/QuACK down-projection backward bridge succeeded on GH200. JAX-owned tensors via zero-copy DLPack ran the down-backward bucket at `1.008ms` for the full shape, making it a credible custom-call target rather than a production bridge by itself.
- 2026-05-13: CuTe DSL through `cutlass.jax.cutlass_call` succeeded on the GH200 worker (`max_abs=0`, `0.118ms` steady for a vector-add smoke), so the source-level CuTe/JAX port path is available.
- 2026-05-14: raw Sonic jax-triton gather/combine with a custom VJP beat the XLA combine proxy in a train-step-shaped GH200 harness, but the QuACK/CuTe down-backward path hit `Unexpected index` lowering failures.
- 2026-05-19: PR #5718 was narrowed to production-visible `implementation="sonic"`: existing concat W13 layout and JAX `ragged_dot` grouped GEMMs, plus raw Sonic jax-triton gather/combine. CuTe/QuACK dependencies and pseudo-Sonic XLA/down-gather public backends were removed from that PR.

## Negative Results Index

- Full W13 custom VJP around the expert-padded path was too broad and slow; the narrower unpack-backward VJP was the useful part. See https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4416373304 and https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4416387690.
- Isolated gather/sum Pallas Triton variants, including faithful source ports and inline PTX arithmetic, did not match real Sonic. The remaining gap persisted even in a standalone Marin-free repro and showed worse SASS/register/control-instruction characteristics for Pallas.
- Directly launching the exact Sonic Triton cubin through JAX FFI worked functionally but carried an approximately fixed `56-60us` launch tax, erasing the Sonic advantage for the isolated gather/sum kernel.
- Mosaic GPU high-level vector indexing currently hits JAX lowering blockers for the relevant metadata/gather forms. Scalar `plgpu.load` workarounds lower but are tied-to-slower than Pallas Triton and remain slower than real Sonic.
- JAX checkpoint/remat with `prevent_cse=False` gave a misleading `4.056ms` result. With `prevent_cse=True`, the best JAX remat path is `5.844ms`.
- Naive activation+W13 fusion in Pallas/Triton is a dead end for this shape: fused `dx` and `dw` subkernels are `14-15ms` each because they recompute the activation derivative per matmul tile.
- Pure JAX whole-MoE `custom_vjp` does not improve schedule quality by itself. The corrected scaffold ran `12.804ms fwd_bwd` and `14.430ms remat_bwd`; making W2 transposes explicit was worse.
- QuACK/CuTe ragged TMA is fragile in this integration. The d-gated epilogue has a two-extra-dim encoding workaround, but the production PR removed the CuTe/QuACK dependency path rather than relying on it.

## Current Conclusion

Forward-only performance and isolated combine microbenchmarks are no longer the main decision point. The practical production path is the narrowed `implementation="sonic"` backend from PR #5718: concat W13 layout, existing JAX `ragged_dot` grouped GEMMs, and raw Sonic jax-triton gather/combine with a custom VJP. The CuTe/QuACK custom-call route remains useful research context but is too fragile for the current production PR. Next work should validate the sonic backend on real GPU training shapes and resolve any remaining robustness issues before treating it as a default MoE path.

## Links

- SonicMoE repo: https://github.com/Dao-AILab/sonic-moe
- Active research branch: `codex/sonic-equivalent-pallas`
- Research logbook: `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-pallas-grug.md`
- Handoff doc: `/Users/dlwh/src/marin/scratch/moe-block-decomposition-handoff-20260513.md`
- Related replacement issue: #5609

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Kickoff scout report (`exploratory`):

- SonicMoE is promising as a source of MoE algorithm ideas, but not as a drop-in backend for Marin. The published stack is PyTorch + Triton + CuTeDSL + QuACK, so a direct JAX integration would imply a separate custom-op path.
- The ideas that look worth scouting in Grug are narrower and more portable: gather-fused grouped GEMM, activation-memory bookkeeping that avoids large `O(T*K*D)` saved intermediates, `w13` / `w2` layout handling, and gather-and-sum vs scatter-first aggregation.
- The current Grug implementation already has the right seams for this work in `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py`: local compact dispatch, EP ring dispatch/collect, and the ragged-all-to-all alternative.
- That means the first tranche should be benchmark-only probes in the existing Grug harness, measured on the same cells that mattered in #3717, #3752, #3821, #3841, #4406, and #4427, before any kernel work is chosen.

Pinned local artifact:
- `.agents/logbooks/sonic-moe-jax-grug-scout.md`

Next:
- write the paper-to-code map from SonicMoE claims to current Grug hot paths
- define the exact benchmark matrix and stop criteria for any SonicMoE-inspired variant
- only escalate to custom-call / Triton / Pallas discussion if a pure JAX benchmark-only probe shows real headroom

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read AGENTS.md, fix-issue, pull-request skills
- [x] Fetch issue #5328 + chained issues (#3420, #4427, #3445, #2710, #3821, #4406, #3431)
- [x] Actionability check — multi-session research scout, not a self-contained bug fix; no PR
- [x] Read `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py`, locate SonicMoE-relevant call sites
- [x] Post paper-to-code map + first benchmark tranche for human review

# Scope

Research scouting (multi-session, design-heavy) — no PR opened per agent rules. Output is a paper-to-code map and a proposed first benchmark tranche on top of the kickoff in [#5328 (comment)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4355849477).

# Paper-to-code map (SonicMoE claim → Grug call site)

Source: [`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py).

- **gather-fused grouped GEMM**
  - site: [`grug_moe.py#L102-L108`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L102-L108) materializes `x_sort = x[token_ids_sort]` before [`grug_moe.py#L131`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L131) `ragged_dot(x_dispatch, moe_w13, group_sizes)`
  - JAX-portable variant: pass `(x, token_ids_sort, group_sizes)` to a gather-fused wrapper around `ragged_dot` so `x_sort` is never materialized. Pure-JAX first; only escalate to Pallas/custom-call if XLA refuses to fuse.
- **activation-memory growth in backward**
  - dominators: explicit checkpoints at [`L128`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L128) (`grug_moe_dispatch_input`, `T*K*D`), [`L131`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L131) (`grug_moe_expert_hidden`, `T*K*I2`), [`L134-L137`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L134-L137) (`grug_moe_dispatch_output`, `T*K*D`)
  - JAX-portable variant: flip remat policy so `grug_moe_dispatch_input` is recomputed from `(x, token_ids_sort)` instead of saved. Mirrors SonicMoE's save-indices-recompute-gather pattern. Pure JAX, measurable today.
- **gather-and-sum vs scatter-first aggregation**
  - scatter-first sites: [`L140`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L140) `at[token_dispatch].add` (local) and [`L429-L432`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L429-L432) `at[token_local].add` + `psum_scatter` (ring-EP)
  - gather-and-sum reference already in tree: [`L218-L230`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L218-L230) `_unpermute_from_global_expert` `einsum("tkd,tk->td")`. Probe: swap the local scatter-add for a gather-and-sum unpermute on the same EP4 cell #3420 used.
- **`w13` / `w2` layout handling**
  - shapes pinned at [`L116-L117`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L116-L117) (`moe_w13: [E D I2]`, `moe_w2: [E I D]`). #3821 / #4406 already explored padded `w13`; reuse those harnesses.

Out of scope for first tranche (CUDA-specific): Torch custom ops, Triton/CuTeDSL kernels, QuACK interfaces, Hopper/Blackwell async-store details.

# Constraints from prior negative results

- #3420 — local `scatter-add` is the durable TPU hotspot, but every Python/JAX return-path rewrite tested regressed against `scatter_psum_scatter` (2.069M tok/s on EP4 `v5p-8`). A gather-and-sum probe must measure on that exact cell or it is not credible.
- #4427 — post-#4297 H100x8 residual is communication/synchronization, not local FC1; SonicMoE's gather-fused GEMM targets local FC1, so the GPU win window on the `262144` cell is narrow (Triton at `26.1M tok/s`, Megatron forward at `33.1M tok/s`). Memory-side wins are the larger lever.
- #3431 — fused TPU forward kernel sat ~7.4x behind XLA. Do not redo any fused-forward kernel without a fundamentally different starting point.

# Proposed first benchmark tranche (pure-JAX, benchmark-only)

All on the existing Grug benchmark harness used in #3420 and #4427.

1. **Activation-memory remat policy probe.** Keep current scatter-first path; flip remat on `grug_moe_dispatch_input` (save→recompute), then on `grug_moe_dispatch_output`. Measure peak HBM and tok/s on EP4 `v5p-8` (#3420 cell) and H100x8 `262144` (#4427 cell). Stop if no peak-HBM reduction at iso tok/s ≥ -2%.
2. **Gather-and-sum unpermute swap on the local return path.** Replace [`L140`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L140) with a `_unpermute_from_global_expert`-style gather+einsum. Same two cells. Stop unless ≥ +0.5% over `scatter_psum_scatter` baseline on TPU EP4 and ≥ +0.5% on H100 exact-cap.
3. **Gather-fused FC1 probe.** Drop explicit `x_sort` materialization at [`L102-L108`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L102-L108); pass indices through a wrapper around `ragged_dot`. Measure on H100x8 `262144` (vs `triton` = `26121235.17 tok/s` from #4427). Stop unless ≥ +3% at parity HBM — #4427 already says local-FC1 headroom is small.
4. **`w13` / `w2` layout sweep.** Only if (1)–(3) leave a gap; replay #3821-style padded `w13` on top of the post-#4297 baseline. #4406 said this no longer adds lift on the shared exact-cap surface, so this rung is contingent.

Whole-scout stop: if (1)–(3) give no measurable win at parity HBM/throughput on either cell, seal as negative and do not escalate to custom-call / Triton / Pallas.

# Open questions for the human

- Confirm the canonical cells: #3420 EP4 `v5p-8` and #4427 H100x8 `262144`, or a newer authoritative cell?
- Gather-and-sum probe scope: local non-EP only, or also the ring-EP return path (where `psum_scatter` still must happen)?
- For the remat policy probe, is the user-visible knob a JAX `checkpoint_policy` or a Grug-level config that should select the policy at the model layer?

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Custom-VJP sidecar for the expert-padded W13 path is a negative result.

I tried the easy version of the padded-unpack replacement: keep the existing pack -> BMM -> unpack forward, but define a custom VJP that computes `dL/dlhs` and `dL/drhs` with XLA `ragged_dot_general` instead of autodiff materializing the padded unpack scatter. Local value/gradient checks passed, but the GH200 006a-like W13 backward microbench is much slower:

- Job: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-padded-custom-vjp-006a-20260510-141312`
- Shape: `T=8192`, `D=2048`, `I=3072`, `E=8`, top-2, BF16, `local_expert_capacity=3072`
- Existing autodiff through padded op: `2.775ms` steady
- Custom VJP via generic XLA ragged dots: `10.130ms` steady

I kept this as a benchmarkable sidecar helper and left production on normal autodiff. The takeaway is that the next serious attempt should be an actual grouped-GEMM/token-broadcast kernel that owns the SonicMoE metadata directly, not a generic `ragged_dot_general` VJP rewrite.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Follow-up: the full W13 custom VJP was bad, but the narrower unpack-backward kernel is promising.

I added a benchmark-only Pallas Triton direct-store kernel for the isolated expert-padded `unpack_bwd` hotspot. It writes `dout[row, col]` directly to `packed_grad[gather_indices[row], col]` for valid rows, relying on the unique padded indices we measured for the 006a-like shape.

GH200 results, 006a-like BF16 W13 backward shape (`T=8192`, `D=2048`, `I=3072`, `E=8`, top-2, `local_expert_capacity=3072`):

- XLA scatter-add `unpack_bwd`: `1.002ms` steady
- XLA scatter-set `unpack_bwd_set`: `1.000ms` steady
- Pallas direct-store `unpack_bwd_pallas`, 64x64: `0.392ms` steady
- Pallas direct-store `unpack_bwd_pallas`, 64x128: `0.384ms` steady
- Pallas direct-store `unpack_bwd_pallas`, 128x128: `0.386ms` steady

All variants were exact against the XLA scatter-add reference. Next step is to promote this as a custom VJP on just the padded-unpack sub-op, then rebench whole padded-W13 backward and a short end-to-end 006a run to see whether the isolated ~0.6ms/call gain survives in context.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Promoted the promising piece narrowly and got a whole-W13-backward win.

Change shape: custom VJP is now only around the expert-padded unpack sub-op on GPU. Forward stays the same; non-GPU keeps ordinary autodiff. The earlier full-W13 custom VJP via generic `ragged_dot_general` remains benchmark-only and is not used in production.

Validation:

- Local tests: `test_sonic_moe.py` plus expert-padded W13 value/gradient tests passed (`7 passed`)
- GH200 job: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-padded-production-vjp-006a-20260510-142949`
- Shape: 006a-like BF16 W13 backward, `T=8192`, `D=2048`, `I=3072`, `E=8`, top-2, `local_expert_capacity=3072`
- Old autodiff through padded unpack: `2.768ms` steady
- Production Pallas-unpack VJP: `2.207ms` steady
- Gradients matched exactly in the harness

So the isolated `unpack_bwd` gain survives as about a 20% whole padded-W13-backward microbench improvement (`~0.56ms` absolute here). Next useful check is a strict no-profiler end-to-end 006a run, then a short profile to verify the old scatter hotspot actually shrinks.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 End-to-end smoke confirms the unpack-subop VJP is a small real training win.

Strict 1x GH200 synthetic 006a-style run after wiring the Pallas unpack-backward VJP:

- Job: `/dlwh/moe-gh200-010c-grug006a-pallas-unpack-noprof-20260510-143326`
- W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/moe-gh200-010c-grug006a-pallas-unpack-noprof-20260510-143326
- Shape: `D=2048`, `L=24`, `I=3072`, shared `I=3072`, `E=8`, top-2, `seq=1024`, `batch=8`, Adam, BF16 params/compute/output, CE=XLA, profiler/HLO logging off
- Result: parent and child succeeded, zero failures/preemptions

Warm rows (`global_step >= 3`):

- Pre-change strict Grug 010a: `0.4455s/step`, `18,388 tokens/s`, `217,890 GFLOP/s`, `22.02%` BF16 MFU
- New Pallas-unpack path 010c: `0.4332s/step`, `18,909 tokens/s`, `224,065 GFLOP/s`, `22.64%` BF16 MFU

That is about a 2.8% end-to-end throughput improvement on this shape. It is not the whole MoE gap, but it is a real win from replacing a profiled scatter hotspot. Next check should be a short profile to verify the old `input_scatter_fusion_73`-like component shrinks, then continue toward the larger grouped-GEMM/token-broadcast port.

comments.body:
🤖 Timing caveat update: the previous table mixed timing methods. Grug/JAX was measured as Python wall time around a `jax.jit` call plus `block_until_ready`; upstream SonicMoE was measured with CUDA events around the Triton launch.

I reran the exact `T=8192`, `K=2`, `H=2048`, `E=8`, BF16 token gather/broadcast shape with upstream SonicMoE reporting both CUDA-event time and synchronized Python wall time. Job: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-token-wallcheck-006c-20260510-174702`.

| Path | Weighted forward combine | Unweighted backward broadcast |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Grug/JAX XLA wall | `0.0938ms` | `0.0935ms` |
| Grug/JAX Pallas Triton wall | `0.1043ms` | `0.1079ms` |
| Upstream SonicMoE Triton CUDA event | `0.0514ms` | `0.0502ms` |
| Upstream SonicMoE Triton wall | `0.0629ms` | `0.0613ms` |

Updated interpretation: dispatch/timing overhead explains part of the earlier `~2x` headline. Matched wall-clock still leaves a real gap: upstream SonicMoE is `~1.5x` faster than Grug/XLA and `~1.7x` faster than the current Grug/Pallas Triton kernel on this isolated path. To attribute the remaining `~31-47us` entirely to device code quality, we still need a JAX kernel-duration-only profile.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 GH200 whole-block/backward decomposition update for the SonicMoE-style Grug MoE path.

Goal for this pass was to find a JAX/Pallas/custom-call route within roughly 10-20% of upstream Sonic/QuACK on the local MoE block, especially by amortizing around whole-block backward rather than only isolated gather/combine kernels.

Baseline full-block proxy, 1x GH200 on CoreWeave RNO2A, `T=8192`, `H=2048`, `I=3072`, `E=8`, top-2, BF16, unique top-k:

| Path | `fwd_bwd` | `fwd2_bwd` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Upstream Sonic/QuACK | `3.428ms` | `4.428ms` |
| Grug scatter | `4.035ms` | `5.910ms` |
| Grug Sonic metadata + XLA combine | `4.296ms` | `5.799ms` |
| Grug Sonic metadata + Pallas combine | `4.277ms` | `5.640ms` |

Job: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-full-block-decomp-20260513-003600`. Best Grug path is still `+0.607ms / +17.7%` on `fwd_bwd`, but `+1.212ms / +27.4%` on `fwd2_bwd`, so we do not have a parity path for both proxies.

Backward decomposition says the remaining gap is not just local combine/scatter dispatch overhead:

| Bucket | Time |
| --- | ---: |
| combine_bwd | `0.430ms` |
| w2_bwd | `0.770ms` |
| activation_bwd | `0.295ms` |
| w13_bwd_materialized | `1.425ms` |
| w13_bwd_materialized_with_xscatter | `1.687ms` |
| w13_bwd_sonic generic helper | `9.988ms` |

Job: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-grug-bwd-parts-20260513-003600`. The implied xscatter component is only about `0.262ms`, so deleting that alone cannot close the full `fwd_bwd` gap. The target needs to be the whole W13 backward + scatter/materialization boundary. The generic Sonic-style W13 helper is a hard negative.

Forward-side buckets are not the main issue:

| Bucket | Time |
| --- | ---: |
| routing metadata | `0.0846ms` |
| routing metadata + xsort | `0.152ms` |
| Sonic metadata, XLA style | `0.0935ms` |
| Sonic metadata, Pallas style | `0.0960ms` |
| W2 + combine, XLA | `0.470ms` |
| W2 + combine, Pallas combine | `0.469ms` |
| combine forward, XLA | `0.115ms` |
| combine forward, Pallas Triton | `0.105ms` |

Jobs: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-grug-forward-parts-20260513-004000`, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-grug-forward-parts-safe-20260513-004430`, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-grug-forward-rest-20260513-004705`. W13-forward microbench variants were unstable on GH200/JAX and hit CUDA illegal address in a `_lambda_` launch, but full forward/full-block runs are healthy enough that this should not be the next focus.

Expert-padded W13 remained a partial win only at the sub-op level:

| Padded W13 backward piece | Time |
| --- | ---: |
| pack | `0.391ms` |
| expert BMM | `0.863ms` |
| unpack_bwd XLA scatter-add | `1.004ms` |
| unpack_bwd Pallas direct-store | `0.403ms` |
| padded_dot_bwd_autodiff | `2.779ms` |
| padded_dot_bwd_production | `2.214ms` |

Job: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-padded-bwd-decomp-20260513-075059`. The direct-store VJP still saves about `0.56ms` inside padded W13 backward, but when wired into the whole-block path it regresses: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-full-block-padded-w13-20260513-081533` gives `fwd_bwd=4.784ms`, `fwd2_bwd=6.499ms` with `--w13-local-expert-capacity 3072`. I added that harness knob as `--w13-local-expert-capacity` for `--mode moe_block`, but this is not the speed path for this shape.

Other negative paths:

| Attempt | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Gather-W13 whole block | `/dlwh/sonicmoe-gather-w13-block-20260513-075328`: `12.696-15.994ms` `fwd_bwd`, `14.212-20.608ms` `fwd2_bwd`; Pallas variants also had numerical differences. |
| Force XLA ragged-dot | `/dlwh/sonicmoe-ragged-dot-impl-block-20260513-080049`: default/Triton `fwd_bwd ~= 4.14-4.17ms`; XLA `22.446ms`. |
| Runtime tile env knobs for Pallas ragged-dot | Multiple CUDA illegal-address crashes; helper refactor reverted, and `git diff -- lib/haliax/src/haliax/nn/ragged_dot.py` is empty. Runtime env helpers perturb lowering and are not a valid tuning mechanism. |
| Static `block_k=64` source edit | `/dlwh/sonicmoe-static-k64-full-block-20260513-081737`: `fwd_bwd=4.648ms`, `fwd2_bwd=6.291ms`; worse than default, reverted. |

A post-revert full-block sanity run, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-full-block-post-tile-20260513-081337`, got scatter `fwd_bwd=4.280ms`, `fwd2_bwd=5.907ms`, confirming the main path is healthy after the failed tile experiments.

Current conclusion: this is not primarily unavoidable host dispatch overhead. The viable Grug path is already using the Pallas/Triton ragged-dot backend on GPU; the XLA ragged-dot backend is unusably slow. The remaining gap looks like device/layout quality around W13 backward plus dx scatter/materialization, especially under remat/whole-block composition. The next useful work is a specialized W13 backward kernel/custom-call that owns Sonic metadata and the dx writeback boundary together. Forward combine, padded W13 as a whole-block replacement, gather-W13, XLA ragged-dot, and runtime tile tuning are all dead ends for this shape.

Local handoff with the detailed command/job trail: `/Users/dlwh/src/marin/scratch/moe-block-decomposition-handoff-20260513.md`.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Remat follow-up: the earlier `fwd2_bwd` gap is mostly a pessimistic proxy artifact for the JAX path.

I added a benchmark mode to `.agents/scripts/sonicmoe_pallas_grug_bench.py`: `--block-measure remat_bwd`. It wraps the differentiated `moe_mlp` forward in `jax.checkpoint(..., prevent_cse=False)`. This is actual JAX remat; the old `fwd2_bwd` mode was a manual extra stop-gradient forward plus ordinary forward/backward.

GH200 job: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-remat-block-20260513-170325`, same `T=8192`, `H=2048`, `I=3072`, `E=8`, top-2, BF16, unique top-k shape.

| Backend | `fwd_bwd` | `fwd2_bwd` proxy | `remat_bwd` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `scatter` | `4.015ms` | `5.707ms` | `4.264ms` |
| `sonic_xla` | `4.254ms` | `5.769ms` | `4.317ms` |
| `sonic_pallas` | `4.061ms` | `5.583ms` | `4.056ms` |

Interpretation: actual JAX remat does not pay the full extra-forward tax that `fwd2_bwd` implied. For the best Sonic-style JAX local path, `remat_bwd` is effectively equal to ordinary `fwd_bwd` in this harness. The right next comparison is against an equivalent real-remat Sonic/PyTorch measurement; do not use the old `fwd2_bwd` proxy as evidence that JAX remat is inherently 27% behind.

I also updated the local handoff: `/Users/dlwh/src/marin/scratch/moe-block-decomposition-handoff-20260513.md`.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: honest remat and activation+W13 fusion both sharpen the current SonicMoE gap.

Scope: 1x GH200 on CoreWeave RNO2A, local full MoE shape `tokens=8192`, `hidden=2048`, `intermediate=3072`, `experts=8`, `topk=2`, BF16. Confidence: `exploratory`, but the negative result is decisive for this Pallas/Triton fusion shape.

Current comparison point:

| Measure | Real Sonic/QuACK | Best JAX/Grug path so far | Gap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| forward | `1.260ms` | `1.285ms` | `+2.0%` |
| `fwd_bwd` | `3.428ms` | `4.035ms` | `+17.7%` |
| `remat_bwd` / checkpoint | `4.798ms` | `5.844ms` with `prevent_cse=True` | `+21.8%` |

Important correction: the earlier JAX `remat_bwd=4.056ms` number used `jax.checkpoint(..., prevent_cse=False)`, so XLA could reuse work across the checkpoint. I changed the harness to `prevent_cse=True`; the honest forced-recompute result is `/dlwh/sonicmoe-jax-remat-prevent-cse-20260513-173642`:

| Backend | `prevent_cse=True remat_bwd` |
| --- | ---: |
| `scatter` | `5.950ms` |
| `sonic_xla` | `5.919ms` |
| `sonic_pallas` | `5.844ms` |

Real Sonic comparison jobs:

- `/dlwh/sonicmoe-real-forward-probe-20260513-172328`: forward `1.260ms`
- `/dlwh/sonicmoe-full-block-decomp-20260513-003600`: `fwd_bwd 3.428ms`, `fwd2_bwd 4.428ms`
- `/dlwh/sonicmoe-real-remat-successenv-20260513-172510`: `remat_bwd 4.798ms`

I also tried fusing activation-gradient derivation into W13 backward in Pallas/Triton:

| Backend/config | Steady |
| --- | ---: |
| `activation_w13_bwd_materialized_with_xscatter`, row 128 / k 64 / hidden 128 | `1.836ms` |
| `activation_w13_bwd_fused`, row 128 / k 64 / hidden 128 | `29.361ms` |
| split fused `dx` scatter | `14.129ms` |
| split fused `dw` | `15.318ms` |
| hybrid materialized gradient + direct `dx` scatter | `1.740ms` vs `1.839ms` baseline |

Jobs: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-activation-w13-fused-smoke-20260513-185934`, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-activation-w13-fused-smoke2-20260513-190102`, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-activation-w13-fused-full-20260513-190204`, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-activation-w13-split-full-20260513-190356`, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-activation-w13-hybrid-full-20260513-190623`.

Interpretation: naive activation+W13 fusion is a dead end. It avoids materializing `d_w13_out`, but recomputes the SwiGLU derivative across many matmul tiles, making both fused subkernels `14-15ms`. The only useful piece is the already-known direct `dx` scatter idea, worth about `0.10ms`, which is not enough to explain the remaining `0.607ms` no-remat gap or `1.046ms` remat gap.

Decision: forward is good enough; no-remat full block is barely within the 10-20% target, but honest remat is just outside it. Further single-boundary Pallas fusions are unlikely to close this. The plausible next paths are a whole-backward custom call / direct Sonic or QuACK backward wrapper, or a profiling pass that proves a specific dispatch/materialization bucket still accounts for the missing time.

Local research logbook updated at `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-pallas-grug.md`; handoff details are in `/Users/dlwh/src/marin/scratch/moe-block-decomposition-handoff-20260513.md`.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: whole-local-MoE `custom_vjp` scaffold is implemented and benchmarked; pure JAX whole-VJP is a negative result for speed.

Goal for this pass: test whether wrapping the full local MoE block in one `jax.custom_vjp` could improve backward scheduling before introducing Sonic/QuACK custom calls.

What changed:

- Added benchmark backend `whole_vjp_xla` in `.agents/scripts/sonicmoe_pallas_grug_bench.py`.
- The forward keeps the Sonic-style expert-sorted layout: gather `x[token_ids_sort]`, grouped W13, SwiGLU, grouped W2, gather-sum combine.
- The backward is one custom VJP returning gradients for `(x, combine_weights, w13, w2)`; routing metadata is nondifferentiable.
- Fixed an initial BF16 mismatch in `dcombine_weights`; the final local BF16 check matches `sonic_xla` to the same tolerance as `scatter` vs `sonic_xla`.

Full-shape GH200 config: `tokens=8192`, `hidden=2048`, `intermediate=3072`, `experts=8`, `topk=2`, BF16, unique top-k, CoreWeave RNO2A.

Corrected scaffold job: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-whole-vjp-xla-fixed-20260513-193921`.

| Measure | `scatter` | `sonic_xla` | `whole_vjp_xla` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `fwd_bwd` | `4.199ms` | `4.336ms` | `12.804ms` |
| `fwd2_bwd` | `5.967ms` | `5.571ms` | `14.236ms` |
| `remat_bwd` | `5.953ms` | `5.792ms` | `14.430ms` |

I also tried making the W2 backward transposes explicit with `ragged_dot_general` dimension numbers. That was worse, not better: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-whole-vjp-xla-direct-20260513-194401` gave `16.950ms fwd_bwd` and `18.749ms remat_bwd` for the whole-VJP path.

Interpretation: the custom-VJP boundary is useful as an ABI/correctness scaffold, but it does not make XLA produce Sonic-like backward code. Pure JAX whole-VJP optimization is not the speed path. To make this approach competitive, the VJP needs to call fewer/larger Sonic/QuACK-shaped backward primitives, especially the `_DownProjection.backward` `gemm_dgated` equivalent and the up-projection/token-broadcast path.

Research logbook updated at `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-pallas-grug.md` under `SONIC-PALLAS-042`.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: Sonic/QuACK down-projection backward is a credible custom-call target; the Torch/DLPack bridge is only an ABI/timing proof.

I added `.agents/scripts/sonicmoe_down_bwd_bridge_bench.py`, a focused harness for the Sonic `_DownProjection.backward` hot section:

- `_down_projection_backward_act(...)`, backed by QuACK `gemm_dgated`, computes `dh`, router-score gradients, and the weighted post-activation operand `a_prime`.
- QuACK `gemm(dout.T, a_prime, cu_seqlens_k=..., A_idx=...)` computes `dw2`.
- Inputs can be Torch-owned or JAX-owned and converted zero-copy to Torch through DLPack.

Full Grug local shape on 1x GH200, `tokens=8192`, `hidden=2048`, `intermediate=3072`, `experts=8`, top-2, BF16:

| Source | Steady |
| --- | ---: |
| Torch-owned tensors | `1.161ms` |
| JAX-owned tensors via zero-copy DLPack | `1.008ms` |

Job: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-down-bwd-bridge-20260513-202747`.

I also fixed the tiny correctness smoke. The first check compared against the wrong GLU layout: Sonic's default preactivation buffer is interleaved `gate0, up0, gate1, up1, ...`, not concatenated `[gate..., up...]`. After fixing the reference, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-down-bwd-bridge-ref4-20260513-133235` succeeded with BF16/accumulation-order scale diffs:

| Grad | max abs | mean abs |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `dh` | `0.5` | `0.00547` |
| `dw2` | `0.125` | `0.01057` |
| `ds` | `1.845` | `0.324` |

The `ds` diff is still the least clean because the PyTorch reference reduces score gradients in a different order from QuACK's colvec-reduce path, but this is no longer the previous layout-scale mismatch.

Why this matters: the bridge bucket is roughly the same conceptual region as the JAX `combine_bwd + w2_bwd + activation_bwd` pieces (`~1.495ms` from the earlier decomposition), so the measured `~1.0ms` QuACK path is a plausible `~0.49ms` win candidate. That is large enough to matter for the remaining no-remat and honest-remat gaps.

Custom-call viability readout:

- QuACK's `gemm_dgated_tuned` and `gemm_tuned` each populated one autotuner cache entry after the call.
- QuACK compiles CuTe DSL kernels with TVM-FFI enabled and persists exported `.o` files via `compiled_fn.export_to_c(..., function_name="func")`; later runs load them via `cute.runtime.load_module(..., enable_tvm_ffi=True)`.
- The DLPack/Torch bridge is not a production JAX training solution because it is outside JIT and depends on Python/Torch runtime ownership.
- The production route should be either a source-level CuTe DSL port callable from JAX with `cutlass.jax.cutlass_call`, or an XLA FFI handler that launches the QuACK TVM-FFI/exported object code on JAX's CUDA stream. A larger whole-backward custom call may be needed if per-subkernel FFI overhead repeats the earlier isolated-gather custom-call tax.

Research logbook updated under `SONIC-PALLAS-043` in `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-pallas-grug.md`.

🤖 Follow-up: the CuTe DSL -> JAX integration path works on the GH200 worker.

I added `.agents/scripts/sonicmoe_cutlass_jax_probe.py`, a small vector-add smoke that defines a CuTe DSL kernel and calls it from `jax.jit` via `cutlass.jax.cutlass_call`. This is not the MoE kernel; it is an environment/proof-of-integration check for the source-level QuACK-shaped port path.

GH200 job: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-cutlass-jax-probe-20260513-134609`.

Result:

```json
{

  "compile_inclusive_s": 0.2419552020728588,

  "elements": 1048576,

```

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Correction on the `ds` correctness smoke from the down-backward bridge: the `ds mean_abs=0.324` number was from the wrong reference path, not a Sonic/QuACK mismatch.

I added a direct score-gradient formula to `.agents/scripts/sonicmoe_down_bwd_bridge_bench.py` matching what QuACK's `gemm_dgated` epilogue computes: `sum_i postact_i * (dout @ W2)_i` in fp32 before score scaling. Follow-up job `/dlwh/sonicmoe-down-bwd-ds-check-20260513-135614`:

| Reference | `ds` max abs | `ds` mean abs | relative RMS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 autograd/scatter reference | `1.845` | `0.324` | `0.00417` |
| direct fp32 epilogue formula | `9.16e-05` | `1.68e-05` | `2.18e-07` |

So the bridge's score gradient is effectively exact against the right mathematical reference. The earlier number is still useful as evidence that the naive PyTorch BF16 reference is not the right checker for `ds`, but it should not be treated as a correctness concern for the QuACK bucket.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Milestone update for the GH200 Sonic-equivalent JAX path (`SONIC-PALLAS-046`, logbook: `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-pallas-grug.md`).

Shape/hardware: `T=8192,H=2048,I=3072,E=8,topk=2,BF16` on `coreweave-rno2a` GH200.

Current comparison:

| Path | Forward | `fwd_bwd` | honest remat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Real Sonic/QuACK | `1.260ms` | `3.428ms` | `4.798ms` |
| Previous best JAX/Grug | `1.285ms` | `4.035ms` | `5.844ms` |
| JAX + CuTe QuACK down-bwd (`sonic_xla_cutlass_down`) | `~1.285ms` | `3.998ms` | `5.103ms` |

What changed:
- The source-level `cutlass.jax.cutlass_call` port of QuACK down-backward is full speed in isolation: `0.956ms` for `dgated + dw2` at the full shape.
- The first whole-MoE custom VJP attempt was a negative result: `12.599ms` `fwd_bwd`, `14.048ms` `fwd2_bwd`, and remat hit `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`.
- The useful path is now granular: keep normal JAX/XLA dispatch, forward, and W13 backward, but wrap only `activation -> down ragged_dot -> gather_sum` in a custom VJP whose backward launches the QuACK CuTe calls.
- After setting `allow_cuda_graph=False` on the custom calls, `remat_bwd` succeeds at `5.103ms`. `fwd_bwd` remeasured at `3.998ms`, about `16.6%` behind real Sonic and inside the target band.

Open blocker:
- `fwd2_bwd` still fails with `Failed to set CUDA graph kernel node params: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` when the extra forward and custom-call backward coexist in one compiled graph. Disabling CUDA graph capture fixed remat but not fwd2, so this looks like a layout/alias/custom-call contract problem rather than ordinary dispatch overhead.

Interpretation:
- This is the first JAX-in-XLA path that reaches the desired speed band for backward/remat, but I would not call it production-ready until `fwd2_bwd` is stable.
- The remaining gap is probably not just JAX dispatch overhead. The isolated QuACK bucket is fast, but integrated savings are partly eaten by GLU interleave/deinterleave packing and residual XLA W13/backward scheduling.

Next steps:
- Inspect `cutlass.jax` `input_spec`/`output_spec`/layout controls and force the custom-call operands/results to match the CuTe views.
- Quantify full-shape GLU packing overhead directly.
- If layout fixes stabilize fwd2, keep this as the short-term JAX path; otherwise port the Sonic/QuACK W13 side or change the JAX W13 layout so the down-backward call consumes interleaved GLU activations directly.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Follow-up milestone: the speed blocker was mostly W13 GLU layout, not dispatch overhead.

Shape/hardware: `T=8192,H=2048,I=3072,E=8,topk=2,BF16` on `coreweave-rno2a` GH200.

Updated comparison:

| Path | Forward | `fwd_bwd` | honest remat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Real Sonic/QuACK | `1.260ms` | `3.428ms` | `4.798ms` |
| Previous best JAX/Grug | `1.285ms` | `4.035ms` | `5.844ms` |
| JAX + CuTe down-bwd, concat W13 | `~1.285ms` | `3.998ms` | `5.103ms` |
| JAX + CuTe down-bwd, interleaved W13 | `1.244ms` | `3.761ms` | `5.036ms` |

What changed:
- I measured the layout conversion tax directly: `concat -> interleaved` costs `0.315ms`, and `interleaved -> concat` costs `0.186ms` at the full shape.
- I added a benchmark backend that simulates storing W13 in Sonic's interleaved GLU layout. That lets JAX/XLA W13 produce interleaved activations directly and lets the QuACK down-backward custom call return interleaved `d_w13_out` directly, with no runtime pack/unpack around the custom call.
- Forward is value-equivalent to `sonic_xla` in the comparison job (`max_abs_vs_first=0.0`).

Interpretation:
- This reaches the original target on the meaningful measures: `fwd_bwd` is now about `9.7%` behind real Sonic, and honest remat is about `5.0%` behind.
- The remaining fwd+bwd gap is not mainly JAX dispatch overhead; it was mostly a layout mismatch around the Sonic/QuACK down-backward bucket.
- A real implementation should store Grug W13 in interleaved GLU layout, or use a Sonic/QuACK W13 path that naturally emits interleaved GLU activations.

Still unresolved:
- `fwd2_bwd` still crashes. Explicit `cutlass.jax.TensorSpec`, removing GLU pack/unpack, and disabling XLA command buffers did not fix it. With command buffers disabled, the crash moves to `wrapped_gather`, which points to a custom-call/XLA runtime correctness issue rather than the speed path itself.

Next concrete step:
- Prototype a real interleaved-W13 Grug layout path instead of the benchmark-only outside-timed transform, then keep fwd2/debuggability as a separate hardening task.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: moved the near-Sonic JAX path out of the benchmark-only harness and into a production-visible Grug/Levanter backend.

Milestone `SONIC-PALLAS-049`: optional production QuACK down-backward backend.

What changed:
- Added real local MoE implementations in `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py`:
  - `sonic_xla_interleaved_w13`
  - `sonic_pallas_interleaved_w13`

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## Problem

When training over multiple epochs, the data is seen in the same order every epoch. The current shuffling infrastructure (`PermutationDataset`) applies a single fixed permutation and does not reshuffle on restart. There's an existing TODO for this:

https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/permutation.py#L19

This is particularly relevant for DNA experiments where we epoch over small datasets many times.

## Discussion

Some approaches were discussed here: [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1418673157585502370/1473412849916186735)

---
### Epoch reshuffling for multi-epoch training

- [x] Gather context: read current permutation code and related files
- [x] Understand the architecture and plan implementation
- [x] Implement `num_epochs` parameter in `PermutationDataset`
- [x] Update `EraShufflingDataset` to support epochs
- [x] Propagate `num_epochs` to `shuffle()` and `era_shuffle()` helper methods
- [x] Write tests (11 new tests + existing tests verified in diff review)
- [x] Run pre-commit ✅
- [x] Commit and push changes

### Summary

Added a `num_epochs` parameter (default `1`) to both `PermutationDataset` and `EraShufflingDataset`. When `num_epochs > 1`:

- The permutation operates over `num_epochs × dataset_len` elements
- Outputs are mapped back to the original range via modulo (`permutation(index) % dataset_len`)
- Each epoch sees all items in a different order — deterministic and resumable
- The reported `async_len()` is `num_epochs × dataset_len`

The `shuffle()` and `era_shuffle()` convenience methods on `AsyncDataset` forward the new parameter.

- `lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/dataset.py` — `shuffle()` and `era_shuffle()` methods
- `lib/levanter/tests/test_newdataset.py` — 11 new tests covering length, item coverage, reshuffling across epochs, validation, out-of-bounds, and convenience methods

**Testing:** Pre-commit (`./infra/pre-commit.py --all-files --fix`) passes cleanly including Pyrefly type checking. The pytest tests require CUDA (via the transformers/torch dependency chain in the conftest), which is not available in this CI runner. issues.author: wmoss
issues.body:
Iris controller restarts today are driven entirely by `iris cluster controller restart` (see `lib/iris/OPS.md`, `.agents/skills/restart-iris/`) — GCE clusters restart via SSH + `docker restart`, CoreWeave clusters via the Kubernetes API — not by Pulumi. This is an investigation, not a commitment to migrate: the restart flow has safety properties that a naive Pulumi resource-replace would break if not carried over deliberately.

Specifically: the controller keeps local SQLite state plus periodic GCS checkpoints, and restart takes a pre-restart checkpoint and writes a rollout record (image + matching checkpoint ref) so a failed health check can roll back atomically. DB migrations are forward-only and some are destructive, so restoring an old controller image without its paired pre-migration checkpoint breaks. Any Pulumi-driven approach needs to preserve this checkpoint-before-restart / paired-rollback behavior, e.g. by keeping restart-with-rollback as a wrapped CLI step (similar to how `iac.iris.service` wraps a CLI today) rather than modeling the controller as a plain replaceable resource.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Investigation, not a bug fix — no PR. Analysis below; handing off to a human for the migrate/don't-migrate call.

# Research

Confirmed the issue body against the code. `iris cluster controller restart` is a CLI-side choreography around a mechanical platform restart; the safety lives in the CLI, not in the platform primitive.

Forward deploy in [`cli/cluster.py:controller_restart` L1117-1215](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1117-L1215): pre-deploy checkpoint (L1180) → build fresh images (L1182) → write `PENDING` rollout record (L1187) → `restart_controller` (L1199) → on health-check failure `_auto_rollback` to previous image + its pre-deploy checkpoint (L1202) → write `COMMITTED` (L1206). `--rollback` (L1148) reverts to the recorded previous image + checkpoint.

The rollout record is a small state machine in GCS remote state, not in any deploy tool's state; the restarted controller consumes `ROLLBACK_REQUESTED` once on boot and self-clears. Migrations are forward-only and some are destructive, so an old image must boot on its paired pre-migration checkpoint — this is why image and checkpoint are recorded as a pair.

**Relevant code**
- [`cli/cluster.py#L1117`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1117) - restart/rollback choreography (checkpoint, record, restart, auto-rollback)
- [`controller/rollout.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/rollout.py) - `RolloutPhase`/`RolloutRecord`, read/write in GCS remote state
- [`platforms/vm_lifecycle.py#L409`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/vm_lifecycle.py#L409) / [`k8s/controller.py#L517`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/controller.py#L517) - mechanical restart primitives (no safety logic)
- [`controller/migrations/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/migrations) - forward-only, sometimes destructive
- [`iac/iris/service.py#L156-L164`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/src/iac/iris/service.py#L156-L164) - existing CLI-wrap template to reuse

# Proposed approach

Do **not** model the controller as a plain replaceable Pulumi resource. A resource-replace would tear down and recreate around the restart, bypassing the checkpoint/rollout-record choreography and losing atomic rollback on a bad deploy.

Instead reuse the pattern already in [`iac/iris/service.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/src/iac/iris/service.py) (and the sibling finelog migration in #7571): wrap `iris cluster controller restart` in a `command.local.Command` component whose `create`/`update` verb runs the restart CLI and whose `delete` is a no-op (or `stop`, deliberately). Key the resource on the controller image tag plus a code hash so a change triggers `update` = restart-with-rollback; a failed health check propagates as a Command error, and the CLI has already auto-rolled-back. The rollout record stays in GCS remote state so `--rollback` keeps working out-of-band from Pulumi state.

Open questions for the human owner:
- Is the goal declarative *drift correction* (Pulumi restarts when image drifts) or just *inventory* (record the controller in the stack without owning restarts)? The wrapper above gives the former; only the latter avoids Pulumi ever triggering a restart.
- How should a Pulumi `up` that fails its health check and auto-rolls-back report to the operator — hard resource failure, or success-with-warning after rollback?
- Interaction with the manual `restart-iris` skill / direct CLI runs: Pulumi must treat an out-of-band restart as convergent, not as drift to undo.

Scope is a new Pulumi component plus wiring — multi-file design work, so leaving implementation to a human per the migration effort in #7571/#7262.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Investigation result: move Iris controller operations under the shared deploy interface, with Pulumi invoking the existing migration-aware restart transaction. Do not make the controller VM or Kubernetes Deployment a plain replaceable Pulumi resource.

Effort: medium, 2026-08-24. I stopped after the current code, linked PRs, Echo history, and Pulumi documentation converged on the same boundary.

### Current Marin context

The new work changes the operator interface, but not Iris's state-safety requirement:

- [#8537](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8537) provides one command tree for Pulumi applications. The executable merged there is `marin-deploy`, so the exact spelling today is `uv run marin-deploy ...`; adding a `deploy` script alias is independent of this design.
- [`controller restart`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1936313ac7da5e1c4f08c0a1634e24cf66f4e772/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1263-L1532) resolves secrets, checkpoints the live controller, builds and pins images, writes `PENDING`, restarts in place, health-checks, and commits or restores the previous image plus checkpoint. The controller [consumes the rollback request once](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1936313ac7da5e1c4f08c0a1634e24cf66f4e772/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/main.py#L51-L85).
- Pulumi [does not automatically roll back a failed update](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/support/faq/infrastructure/#automatic-rollbacks). Finelog therefore captures the active revision outside Pulumi, runs `pulumi up`, restores on failure, and refreshes state ([#7690](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7690), [current implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1936313ac7da5e1c4f08c0a1634e24cf66f4e772/lib/finelog/src/finelog/deploy/_k8s.py#L390-L471)). Iris needs that recovery boundary and its additional checkpoint pairing.

### Recommended first migration

1. Add a separate `infra/iris` application project with one stack per controller cluster. This follows the repository rule that application deploy lifecycles stay outside the static `infra/pulumi` substrate project.
2. Add an Iris controller component backed by `command.local.Command`. Its `create` and `update` verbs run the existing `iris cluster controller restart`; removal has no stop/delete verb. Inputs include the cluster, reviewed config hash, working-tree hash, and an explicit deploy generation for a forced same-tree restart. Pulumi's command provider runs `update` when inputs/triggers change instead of replacing the resource ([provider contract](https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/command/api-docs/local/command/)).
3. Add service-specific commands:

   ```text
   uv run marin-deploy iris rollout <cluster>
   uv run marin-deploy iris rollout <cluster> --force
   uv run marin-deploy iris rollback <cluster>
   ```

   `rollback` must call the existing `--rollback` path and use the GCS rollout record. Pulumi history is not a substitute for the recorded image/checkpoint pair. The rollout record remains the recovery source of truth; Pulumi records which reviewed tree/config triggered the transaction.
4. Keep the existing fleet gates: clean/current tree preflight, one cluster at a time, baseline snapshot, five-minute verification, and smoke job. Do not add Iris to the parallel path-triggered deployment matrix in the first change. That matrix cannot currently stop the fleet at the first failed cluster, and GCE restarts also require per-user SSH access.

This stage gives Iris the shared `marin-deploy` UX and Pulumi update/audit surface while preserving the current transaction even when an operator runs `pulumi up` directly.

### Native-resource follow-up

A later CoreWeave-only stage can adopt the non-secret runtime objects into an application stack: ConfigMap, protected PVC, Recreate Deployment, Service, PDB, node-agent DaemonSet, LocalQueue, and priority classes. It should proceed only after the deploy driver is split into prepare/activate/finalize/rollback operations and these conditions are tested:

- no workload mutation before a fresh checkpoint and `PENDING` record;
- every activation or health failure restores the recorded image and checkpoint, waits for `ROLLED_BACK`, then refreshes Pulumi state;
- direct `pulumi up` cannot bypass preparation;
- secret values remain outside Pulumi state;
- controller storage is protected, and GCE application changes never replace the controller VM;
- manual break-glass rollback remains convergent with the next intentional rollout.

Confidence is high for the first migration. Native CoreWeave ownership is feasible with those gates, but it is a separate lifecycle refactor; GCE should continue using the in-place SSH restart mechanism behind the same command.

### Handoff

No PR was opened because this request was an investigation. The next decision is whether to implement the first migration as scoped above and track native CoreWeave resource ownership separately.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Build RiffleEval as a paired long-context evaluation of coherent stream tracking. Each base item keeps the source text, question, answer, distractors, and token budget fixed while changing document chunks from blocked to riffled order. The primary result is the per-item riffle penalty, sliced by foreign-chunk interference count and token distance.

UncheatableEval is a candidate source feed after revision pinning, token-length filtering, license review, and safety filtering. Its current Marin integration is unsuitable: it downloads a stale GitHub fork whose records are capped at 5,000 characters and supplies no questions or evidence annotations. For v0, use frozen natural documents with exact-answer factual overlays; evaluate a filtered UncheatableEval `-Long` subset as one source arm, beginning with English Wikipedia and permissively licensed documents.

## Description

Long-context evaluations such as NIAH often test retrieval of one conspicuous item from a large context. RiffleEval tests whether a model can maintain several ordered information streams whose chunks repeatedly alternate across a 32K–64K prompt, then reconstruct facts within one stream.

For source document \(D_i = [C_{i,1}, \ldots, C_{i,n}]\), generate a legal merge that preserves chunk order within each source. Every chunk receives an opaque, per-example stream ID and ordinal. Questions and evidence annotations are created and verified against the clean document before riffling.

Each base item produces these conditions:

1. Clean target document, for source-task competence.
2. Blocked full context, with the target and distractor documents contiguous.
3. Riffled full context, with identical content and prompt budget.
4. Adjacent-evidence control for multi-evidence items.

The v0 task families are single-stream exact QA and two-evidence within-stream integration. Cross-stream joins and continuation NLL remain follow-ups.

The proposed context-length and stream-count matrix is not a full Cartesian product. With 4K–8K source documents, 32K supports roughly 4–8 streams and 64K supports roughly 8–16 streams. Larger documents or additional filler semantics would be required to hold stream count fixed while scaling total context. The generator must reject infeasible cells instead of silently repeating or padding sources.

## Hypothesis or Goal

At fixed content and question difficulty, riffling causes a measurable accuracy loss beyond the loss caused by the same blocked distractors. The loss increases with the number of intervening foreign chunks after controlling for absolute token distance. Better long-context checkpoints should move the retention curve toward larger interference counts.

## Status

Background research is complete. No implementation or model run has started.

### Proposed v0

- 250–500 verified base items, expanded into deterministic paired variants.
- 32K and 64K contexts; feasible 4/8/16-stream cells; approximately 512-token chunks.
- Exact short answers with one-evidence and two-evidence overlays.
- Opaque opening and closing markers with tokenizer-balanced random IDs.
- Random and same-domain distractors.
- Native-model score with tools disabled.
- Exact match, per-item riffle penalty, blocked-to-riffled penalty, and retention curves by token distance, interference count, evidence count, and active streams.
- Target-stream extraction and oracle-evidence diagnostics to separate stream selection from reasoning.
- Frozen generator version, seed, source revision/hash, tokenizer, prompt, and structural metadata for every item.

### UncheatableEval corpus decision

Use it as an optional source-discovery and freshness feed. Do not use the published collection as the sole corpus or reuse `experiments/datasets/uncheatable.py`.

The current upstream `-Long` snapshots contain 7,500 records across 15 categories and retain source URL, date, category, `content`, and `untruncated_content`. They provide recent natural interference, but no question, answer, stable ID, evidence span, or hop graph. The dataset card declares no dataset license, and source rights differ by document. AO3 has safety concerns; arbitrary GitHub files need license and secret checks; BBC is a poor redistribution default; PDF extraction can corrupt arXiv text. Freshness only protects models whose training cutoff predates the crawl.

A derived arm must:

- pin the Hugging Face revision and content hash;
- filter on benchmark-tokenizer length, language, quality, and safety;
- record URL, collection date, source category, license, and transformed-text hash;
- begin with English Wikipedia and individually cleared permissive sources;
- exclude BBC and AO3 from v0;
- generate exact-answer overlays and frozen evidence spans against the exact transformed text.

## Background Research Brief

- Effort / stop rule / date: medium; 2026-08-24; stopped when the internal, benchmark, corpus, and contradiction passes no longer changed the v0 recommendation.

### Current Marin context

- #7638 owns RULER integration. RiffleEval should not duplicate its eval harness work.
- #4736 specified the closest reusable data contract: frozen long-document QA items with exact answers, evidence spans, and length bins.
- #7181 found that retained MRCR context reduced final-turn PPL from 21.0855 to 10.4012 at 8,192 tokens. Its extraction PR #7203 closed unmerged, so it is prior evidence rather than current infrastructure.
- #5825 previously built 32K/64K long-document PPL slices; the implementation was later removed by #6633.
- No existing issue or implementation tests repeated switching among several coherent streams.

### External prior art

- [RULER](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06654) varies context length and task complexity across multi-needle retrieval, variable tracking, aggregation, and QA. RiffleEval adds coherent natural streams and a paired blocked/riffled intervention.
- [MRCR/Michelangelo](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12640) shows that repeated, similar requests and ordinal selection are harder than unique needles. RiffleEval should include similar competing streams and report random/noise floors.
- [NoLiMa](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05167) shows that lexical overlap makes retrieval easier and normalizes long-context scores to short-context competence. RiffleEval should vary lexical overlap and reject items with weak clean-document accuracy.
- [BABILong](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/c0d62e70dbc659cc9bd44cbcf1cb652f-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf) distributes multi-fact synthetic tasks through natural books. RiffleEval adds several foreground streams, explicit stream identities, and the same task before and after structural transformation.
- [LOFT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13121) found that marker and prompt formatting materially affect retrieval. Marker tokenization and query placement must be fixed or explicitly ablated.
- [UncheatableEval](https://github.com/Jellyfish042/uncheatable_eval) evaluates rolling internet text by NLL. Its freshness method is useful for source discovery; it does not provide RiffleEval annotations.

### Contradiction and shortcut pass

- Random riffles and IDs prevent fixed-order contamination but do not prevent a model from answering public facts from parametric memory. Synthetic counterfactual overlays provide the durable control.
- Opaque IDs expose segmentation but do not prevent keyword search within the target stream. Lexical-overlap and near-neighbor distractor slices remain necessary.
- “Uniform-ish” legal merges do not independently control gap length. Sample examples from explicit interference-count and token-distance strata.
- Marker token lengths can differ across tokenizers and become an unplanned treatment. Balance marker encodings and store their token counts.
- Native QA generation from unannotated documents can admit one-passage shortcuts. Require evidence spans, clean-document verification, and minimal-evidence ablations.

### Recommended next experiments

#### 1. Validate the paired structural signal at 32K

- Minimum experiment / baseline: 100 overlay items, four streams, 512-token chunks; clean, blocked, and riffled conditions on two representative models with different long-context capability.
- Expected signal / falsifier: a nonzero blocked-to-riffled penalty that grows across interference buckets while clean accuracy remains high. Near-zero penalty, floor-level clean accuracy, or prompt-format sensitivity larger than the treatment falsifies the current setup.

#### 2. Add two-evidence integration and 64K

- Minimum experiment / baseline: two controlled facts in widely separated chunks; adjacent-evidence and oracle-extracted-stream baselines; feasible 8/16-stream cells.
- Expected signal / falsifier: two-evidence retention degrades faster than one-evidence retention while oracle extraction recovers most accuracy. Failure of the oracle indicates base reasoning or question-construction problems.

#### 3. Compare source pools

- Minimum experiment / baseline: matched overlays over a pinned filtered UncheatableEval `-Long` arm and one stable, license-cleared long-document corpus.
- Expected signal / falsifier: model ranking and riffle penalty remain stable across source pools. Large domain-specific reversals require a multi-corpus benchmark or removal of the unstable source.

### Source ledger

| Source | Type | Location | Claim used for | Confidence | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RULER | paper | https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06654 | complexity axes and baselines | high | nearest variable-tracking precedent |
| Michelangelo / MRCR | paper and official code | https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12640 | repeated similar needles and order | high | conversation format differs from riffled documents |
| NoLiMa | paper | https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05167 | lexical-overlap shortcut and retention normalization | high | single-association retrieval |
| BABILong | paper | https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/c0d62e70dbc659cc9bd44cbcf1cb652f-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf | distributed multi-fact reasoning in natural text | high | one background stream |
| LOFT | paper | https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13121 | formatting and identifier sensitivity | high | fixed retrieval corpora |
| UncheatableEval | official repo and dataset | https://huggingface.co/datasets/Jellyfish042/UncheatableEval-2026-07-Long | source schema, freshness, and corpus limitations | high | no dataset-level license or QA annotations |
| Marin #4736 | GitHub issue | https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4736 | QA manifest and evidence schema | high | closed before implementation |
| Marin #7638 | GitHub issue | https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7638 | active RULER scope | high | avoid duplicate harness work |
| Marin #7181 | GitHub issue | https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7181 | paired MRCR PPL result | high | extraction PR closed unmerged |

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates: #7638, #4736, #7181, #5825

## Decision Log

- 2026-08-24: scope v0 to paired single-stream exact QA and two-evidence within-stream integration at 32K/64K.
- 2026-08-24: treat UncheatableEval as an optional filtered source arm; reject the current Marin handle and the unfiltered published corpus as the canonical benchmark source.
- 2026-08-24: defer cross-stream joins, continuation NLL, and 128K+ until the primary structural signal is validated.

## Conclusion

Open. Advance to implementation if the 32K pilot produces high clean accuracy, a reproducible blocked-to-riffled penalty, and a stable ordering across source pools and marker templates.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
Setup a simple training actor & web service for Levanter runs.

This might start with a recreation of our previous rigging/telltale service - we should have a dashboard with basic training data and server status. In addition, we can have a button to trigger checkpoints on the next step, or trigger a given watcher etc.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Assessment:** Large, open-ended feature (training actor + web service + dashboard + control plane), not a self-contained bug. Per the fix-issue workflow this is design work, so no PR — posting grounding and a proposed approach for a human to scope first. No existing "rigging/telltale" service in the tree (the `telltale`/`rigging` grep hits are unrelated Finelog/Iris terms).

# Research

The hook, metrics, and checkpoint plumbing a training actor needs already exists in Levanter; the missing piece is a small server that reads a per-step snapshot and can request actions on the next step. Two existing pieces are directly reusable: `run_hooks(..., force=True)` already threads a `force` flag down to callbacks, and the checkpointer's `on_step` already honors `force` for on-demand saves — so a "checkpoint now" button is a flag the callback flips, not new checkpoint logic.

**Relevant code**
- [`trainer.py#L141-L144`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L141-L144) — `run_hooks(info, force)` dispatches `on_step(info, force=...)`
- [`trainer.py#L170`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L170) — `add_hook()` registers a `Callback`
- [`checkpoint.py#L548`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L548) — `Checkpointer.on_step(*, tree, step, force)` — force-save path
- [`_iris_status.py#L86-L118`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/callbacks/_iris_status.py#L86) — existing callback surfacing step/loss/throughput/MFU to Iris status
- [`dashboard_server.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/dashboard_server.py) — Starlette dashboard pattern (static bundle + JSON API) to copy

# Proposed approach

1. `TrainingActorCallback(Callback)` registered via `add_hook(every=1)`. Each `on_step` writes an immutable snapshot (step, loss, throughput/MFU, run progress, checkpoint status) and, before returning, reads a request flag; a pending "checkpoint" request forces a save on the next step.
2. A lightweight async server (Starlette + uvicorn, matching `dashboard_server.py`) co-located with the run: `GET /api/status` returns the snapshot; `POST /api/checkpoint` sets the request flag; `POST /api/hook/<name>` triggers a named registered watcher. Serve a minimal static page from `/`.
3. Reuse the tracker/`StepInfo` metrics already computed — do not recompute.
4. Iris actor wrapper is optional; defer until multi-run coordination is actually needed.

# Scoping questions (blockers on a definition of done)

1. **Where does the server run** — in the training process on the lead host (simplest), or as a separate Iris actor coordinating multiple runs? This decides the whole architecture.
2. **Access model** — single-run local dashboard, or a fleet view aggregating many concurrent runs? Auth (IAP-gated like evaldash/grafana, or loopback-only)?
3. **Control surface for v1** — is "status view + checkpoint-on-next-step" the minimum, or must arbitrary watcher/callback triggering ship in the first cut?
4. **Overlap with existing surfaces** — how should this relate to W&B and the Iris task-status reporter already in place? Replace, complement, or embed links?

Happy to implement once (1)-(3) are pinned down; (1) in particular changes the design substantially.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
Some potential improvements we noticed during the hero run rollout.

scatter aggregation:
  - can you run a scatter aggregation step alongside the mappers? for each N map shards finished, read them in and reshuffle/merge the outputs by reduce shard. the inputs should be pre-sorted by target shard, so in theory this can be done with low-memory. this should reduce read traffic by a factor of ~N, and potentially eliminates the external sort we currently do entirely

datafusion as a loading api:
  - supports parquet reading & query push down
  - seems robust from our experience with finelog
  - trivializes a "lite" sql select only API
  - would be nice for library sharing across projects

mapper auto-tuning:
  - choose the number of mappers for the user based on heuristics or dynamically based on observations
  - we have many pipelines that run 10x too slow just because they have fewer mappers than needed
  - combine this with the scatter aggregation to avoid map/reduce shard blowup

better partial recovery:
  - allow recovering a partially complete run
  - for example the zephyr coordinator might write a state record once a minute recording all of the shard state
  - check for this when booting up and reuse it if the ids match

kv-store work scattering:
  - the kv store actors can be used in the some situations to split up imbalanced workloads
  - push the work to the kv store via compute functions

issues.author: claude[bot]
issues.body:
The TPU canary ferry (Grug MoE smoke test) crashes at compile time on the first `train_step`. On this run the crash was deterministic across all 4 task attempts, so `max_task_failures` was exceeded and the job failed.

The expert grouped-matmul fails to lower on TPU v6e: the megablox GMM `pallas_call` builds an output `BlockSpec((512, 32))` for an output array of shape `(524288, 128)`. Pallas requires the last block dim to be divisible by 128 or equal to the array dim; 32 is neither.

```
ValueError: The Pallas TPU lowering currently requires that the last two
dimensions of your block shape are divisible by 8 and 128 respectively, or be
equal to the respective dimensions of the overall array. Block spec for outputs
in pallas_call kernel at .../pallas/ops/tpu/megablox/gmm.py:393 has block shape
(Blocked(block_size=512), Blocked(block_size=32)), array shape (524288, 128)
```

Call path: `levanter/grug/_moe/scatter.py:48` (expert MLP projection), then `haliax.nn.ragged_dot._ragged_dot_megablox_impl` (`lib/haliax/src/haliax/nn/ragged_dot.py:93`), then `jax.experimental.pallas.ops.tpu.megablox.gmm`. The output n=128 equals the canary model intermediate_dim.

Reproduce:
1. Run the TPU canary ferry `python -m experiments.ferries.canary_ferry` on `v6e-4` (`CANARY_MODEL`: hidden_dim=32, intermediate_dim=128, num_experts=32, num_experts_per_token=2, num_layers=4).
2. The failure is intermittent across scheduled runs (history below); it reproduces when the megablox GMM lowers fresh instead of loading from the shared JAX compilation cache.

Expected: the megablox GMM lowers with a valid output block (last dim divisible by 128, or equal to n) and the canary trains to the regression gate.

<details><summary>Root-cause status (unresolved discrepancy)</summary>

The observed tn=32 does not match the checked-out tiling logic. `_megablox_tile_size()` at HEAD returns an n-tile of 1024, so `_ragged_dot_megablox_impl` passes `tiling[2] = min(n=128, 1024) = 128`, which would produce a valid `(512, 128)` output block. Static reading of the current code does not explain how tn=32 was emitted. This gap is the crux and needs a kernel owner.

Signals pointing away from a fresh code regression on the commit for this run:
- The prior scheduled canary (2026-08-27 06:30 UTC, `f8972ac`) succeeded. The three commits since (PR 8721 external eval/RL runtimes, PR 8717 echo dashboard, PR 8710 IAM grant) touch no JAX, haliax, levanter, or grug code.
- `ragged_dot.py` last changed 2026-08-25 (PR 8610), before two successful runs.
- Canary history alternates pass/fail (Aug 26 pass, Aug 27 06:30 pass, 03:42 and 17:21 fail).

The failing attempt logged a compilation-cache read failure immediately before the crash:
```
UserWarning: Error reading persistent compilation cache entry for
jit__create_lm_example: RuntimeError: Session is closed
```
Shared cache: `gs://marin-eu-west4/tmp/ttl=30d/compilation-cache`. Leading hypothesis: a latent megablox tiling incompatibility for these shapes, normally masked by compilation-cache hits and exposed when the cache read fails and the kernel lowers cold. Not confirmed.
</details>

Canary run context:

- Lane: tpu (GCP, TPU v6e-4, europe-west4)
- Iris job: `/runner/iris-run-job-20260827-172216`
- GHA run: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/33097960592
- W&B run: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/canary-tpu-33097960592-1

issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This issue defines a 150-run learning-rate and token-budget sweep for the Aug/Hero MoE setup. It covers six model widths from d512 through d2048, five token budgets from 30x through 600x active parameters, and five LR multipliers around the May-Recipe MuonH recommendation. The goal is to see whether the recommended LR remains compute-optimal as both model size and training tokens scale, or whether the Aug/Hero recipe needs a systematic LR adjustment. Current status: the sweep is specified but no runs have been launched yet.

### Helpful links
- `experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp/sweep.md` on branch `aug_hero_run_ablations`
- #6711
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Model sizes and architecture are fixed by the hero sweep table (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp/sweep.md`, branch `aug_hero_run_ablations`): d512, d768, d1024, d1280, d1536, d2048, each with its local/global KV split and explicit global-attention layers, a 1024-token sliding window, and sequence length 8192. The `60×` column in that table is the reference token budget; the other multipliers just scale the step count (batch is fixed per size).

## Goal

Map the compute-optimal learning rate relative to the May-Recipe heuristic across model size and token budget — i.e. whether the recommended LR holds, or needs a systematic multiplier, as we scale tokens (30×→600×) and width (d512→d2048).

## Sweep

- **Sizes (6):** d512, d768, d1024, d1280, d1536, d2048.
- **Token budgets (5):** 30×, 60×, 150×, 300×, 600× active params. 60× matches `sweep.md`; steps scale linearly.
- **LR multipliers (5):** 0.7, 0.85, 1.0, 1.2, 1.4 × the recommended MuonH LR.
- **Total: 6 × 5 × 5 = 150 runs.**

### Steps per (size × token budget)

| size | batch | 30× | 60× | 150× | 300× | 600× |
|------|------:|----:|----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| d512  |  32 | 2115 |  4230 | 10575 | 21150 |  42300 |
| d768  |  64 | 3172 |  6345 | 15862 | 31725 |  63450 |
| d1024 | 128 | 4170 |  8340 | 20850 | 41700 |  83400 |
| d1280 | 128 | 7547 | 15094 | 37734 | 75469 | 150938 |
| d1536 | 256 | 6238 | 12476 | 31191 | 62381 | 124762 |
| d2048 | 512 | 6221 | 12442 | 31106 | 62212 | 124425 |

### Recommended MuonH LR (1.0×) per (size × token budget)

The heuristic LR falls as tokens grow (`adam_lr ∝ tokens^-0.395`), so the base LR is per (size, token budget); each run multiplies its cell by {0.7, 0.85, 1.0, 1.2, 1.4}.

| size | 30× | 60× | 150× | 300× | 600× |
|------|----:|----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| d512  | 0.0202 | 0.0154 | 0.0107 | 0.0081 | 0.0062 |
| d768  | 0.0174 | 0.0133 | 0.0092 | 0.0070 | 0.0053 |
| d1024 | 0.0161 | 0.0123 | 0.0085 | 0.0065 | 0.0049 |
| d1280 | 0.0123 | 0.0094 | 0.0065 | 0.0050 | 0.0038 |
| d1536 | 0.0139 | 0.0106 | 0.0074 | 0.0056 | 0.0043 |
| d2048 | 0.0143 | 0.0109 | 0.0076 | 0.0058 | 0.0044 |

### Naming

`aug-hero-{size}-{mult}x-lr{lrmult}`, e.g. `aug-hero-d1024-150x-lr0.85`.

## Status

Defined; **no runs launched.**

## Links

- Sweep config: `experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp/sweep.md` (branch `aug_hero_run_ablations`)

Part of #6711
