# Weekly Sync 8/3 - 8/7 ---
Extraction Unit Tests Ran some other benchmarks: Pretty universally it seems like we get way higher recall but lose on precision. HOWEVER I looked into these benchmarks and they reward things like removing titles, authors, copyright info, and comments sections which are all things I deliberately chose to KEEP in the document, so we can either remove copyrightten documents or include interesting discussion about articles. This is not to say that we don't incidentally extract some stuff that is genuine garbage. Sometimes author bios for articles end up being advertisements for something that person wants to sell you, sometimes related articles are not that useful (however sometimes related questions end up being a nice QA style chunk of questions AND their answers so it is an edge case). On our own unit tests we look pretty good. The unit tests are comprised of domain specific evals. 13 code, 10 math, 9 tables, 29 prose, 12 attribution, 5 structure, 24 negative. We are worst at the "negative" case which has to do with removing content. | system | total | code | math | table | prose | attribution | structure | negatives | |---------------|:-------:|:----:|:----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----------:|:---------:|:---------:| | GOLD (self-test) | 102/102 | 13/13 | 10/10 | 9/9 | 29/29 | 12/12 | 5/5 | 24/24 | | **marin v1.1 (ours)** | **90/102** | **13/13** | **10/10** | **9/9** | 28/29 | **12/12** | **5/5** | 13/24 | | resiliparse | 92/102 | 13/13 | 10/10 | 8/9 | 27/29 | 12/12 | 5/5 | 17/24 | | ORIGINAL spec | 84/102 | 13/13 | 9/10 | 7/9 | 24/29 | 8/12 | 5/5 | 18/24 | | Dripper | 84/102 | 13/13 | 7/10 | 9/9 | 26/29 | 2/12 | 4/5 | 23/24 | | trafilatura | 78/102 | 13/13 | 7/10 | 7/9 | 23/29 | 3/12 | 5/5 | 20/24 | https://claude.ai/code/artifact/ccb92af7-09dc-42ae-b37a-0d40aad802b7
---
Mixing Results View Mixes: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/83283a3a-90b4-46a1-b88d-de18510578f4 View Eval Results: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/c283aebd-ed3a-4685-823d-62e8e3a70884 Better version but can't be shared publicly because of script tags: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/dae91143-af49-401c-acac-e3a1627929a5 Note our high coverage spec is still extracting so this is still somewhat preliminary exploration of data mixing. Mixing for 3 Targets: --- **OLMO Base Easy Evals:**
Details Spec-Driven Mix: On the OLMO dev set this was optimized for it is great: Even overall on OLMO full set it is pretty great: However on DCLM Core it doesn't move the needle very much:
--- --- **DCLM Core v2:** Since OLMO dev set optimization didn't move things that much for DCLM maybe optimizing on it directly will?
Details Spec-Driven Mix: Surprisingly it doesn't move DCLM that much, although it makes HQ competitive with DCLM: Fully inverts the OLMO scores though when you mix for DCLM instead:
--- --- **BLEnD Cultural QA:** From here: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.09948
Details Spec-Driven Mix: Interestingly the DCLM data is better for cultural QA than our old spec, but I suspect our new spec will be better: I also suspect this might have more to do with models being good at in-context MCQ than cultural understanding
---
---
The Problem with DCLM Core DCLM Disaggregated: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/dc5f1cf5-eb62-4c99-9e2f-70472b28797e OLMO Disaggregated: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/ce4e61f6-f3e9-433b-ae76-805a12015ee5 DCLM Core is super noisy. Some are higher signal (basically hellaswag), and with mixing we can improve over Hellaswag: But many **many** are just noise, and no sense of trying to win on them at this scale: In contrast OLMO bpb seems to be pretty high signal: Although there are some that are still noisy here too: My thought: **maybe we forget about DCLM Core and showcase wins on OLMO Base Easy instead at least for spec-driven project at smaller scale** This is where we already win, no new specs, no mixing needed!
---
Distillation Progress Distilling back into our FastText -> ModernBERT -> Resiliparse/JustText pipeline for LLM_Curated_v1.1. **FastText**: **ModernBERT**: Still training - ModernBERT 1M: 40.3% (step 1,575 / 3,906) — on pace to finish tonight, F1 lands right after in its end-of-run eval. - ModernBERT 10M: 11.1% (step 4,317 / 39,062) — the multi-day flagship, pace steady at ~5s/step, ETA roughly 2 days out. **Resiliparse (instead of JustText since it is faster)**:
---
Plan **Experiment Idea**: Scale everything down by 20x. So instead of a 100B model we are training a 5B, and instead of nemotron producing 7T tokes we sample 350B tokens. And instead of a 2T token target or similar we have a 200B token target. Once I extract 5% of the internet I will have about 3-4T tokens or so. We would be comparing 350B tokens of nemotron to 2T tokens of my data, on a 200B token target for a 5B model. We can do whatever data mixing we choose but at the end of the day we need to find the best 200B tokens to train that 5B model. This seems like the most fair way to compare the data at smaller scale and should be achievable within a week or so of launching my big run.
---

# Wednesday August 12th Sync Today I intend to talk about: - How for the scale we are working at we should move away from DCLM Core v2 (until we can do some larger scale runs) - The two main thrusts I have been iterating on: **data mixing** and **pipeline distillation** - The current status of the 10k extraction - Some planning for what we should prioritize next Some of this is overlap with the notes I added to the thread last Friday, but this should be a cleaner version --- > [!NOTE] > This should be the **final** week we have to look at old "high_quality" results rather than the new "llm_pipeline_v1.1" spec ---
Why possibly we should ditch DCLM (for this scale) Full Viewer: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/dae91143-af49-401c-acac-e3a1627929a5 Unfortunately because it includes javascript Anthropic won't let me share it publicly. **GENERAL THOUGHTS ABOUT DCLM CORE v2**: From [Olmo 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.13961): Recommendation from chatting with David Heineman: - BPB based evals are higher signal for models under around 10^22 flops - Above this threshold you can switch to accuracy based evals but need to average over a large set **WHERE WE ARE AT WITH DCLM CORE v2**: Even when I mix directly for it **high_quality** does not exceed **DCLM** (note we are still just a bit out from getting **llm_pipeline_v1.1** which could change things). But when we disaggregate... There is a lot of noise: It is not all noise though: **IF WE TURN TO OLMO BASE EASY (which is bpb based)**: Without mixing we might already be the best or tied for the best: Closer look: After mixing we are FULLY better:
**TAKEAWAY** > [!TIP] > I think we need to do one of three things going forward: > - Convert DCLM Core to a BPB based eval > - Ignore the results at this scale and collect enough data to realistically train a 10^22 flop model for comparison > - Switch to trusting the OLMO Base Easy results instead ---
Data Mixing The Data Mixing setup seems to be working. We are getting clear benefits on what we mix towards: **OLMO Base Easy** **DCLM CORE** **BLEnD** NOTE with Blend I spoke with Will Held yesterday and I am not setting up the evals properly so this one needs to be rerun.
How I currently run it ``` The following are questions about everyday life in South Korea. Question: What is a common snack for preschool kids in South Korea? Answer: cookie Question: What is a popular food to go with beer in South Korea? Answer: fried chicken Question: What is the most popular fruit in South Korea? Answer: apple Question: What is a common school cafeteria food in South Korea? Answer: kimchi Question: What is a popular snack at an amusement park in South Korea? Answer: churros Question: What is a popular afterschool sport for elementary schools in South Korea? Answer: ``` **Take the logprobs of the correct answer** -- this comes from OLMO base easy multiple choice scoring
How I should be running it ``` The following are questions about everyday life in South Korea. What is a common snack for preschool kids in South Korea? A. cilok B. cookie C. egg D. jam sandwiches Answer: B. cookie What is a popular food to go with beer in South Korea? A. fritter B. kimchi C. pizza D. tea Answer: B. kimchi What is a popular snack at an amusement park in South Korea? A. churros B. cotton candy C. crisps D. shawarma Answer: A. churros What is a popular afterschool sport for elementary schools in South Korea? A. American Football B. hide and seek C. soccer D. stick game Answer: ``` **Take the logprobs of letter and answer** -- something Will figured out from scaling MMLU
The movement from the BLEnD mix is sensible: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/83283a3a-90b4-46a1-b88d-de18510578f4 HQ: DCLM:
**TAKEAWAY** > [!TIP] > Our Olmix clone works for getting data mixes that better steer towards particular benchmarks > > However, **high_quality** is not better than **dclm** after mixing at all benchmarks. We need to see if our coverage bet played off for **llm_pipeline_v1.1** when that is ready next week. ---
Pipeline Distillation **RESILIPARSE AUTORESEARCH**
MANY Benchmarks ### marin devset v2 — 420 docs, token-F1 | Extractor | F1 | P | R | |---|--:|--:|--:| | **This fork (0177)** | **0.9050** | 0.8673 | 0.9462 | | Dripper | 0.8943 | 0.8917 | 0.8969 | | resiliparse (upstream) | 0.8880 | 0.8451 | 0.9355 | | trafilatura (upstream) | 0.8518 | 0.9075 | 0.8026 | per-doc: mean 0.8927 · median 0.9491 · ≥0.90: 283/420 · ≥0.80: 356/420 · <0.50: 17/420 ### WebMainBench en/dev — 200 docs, token-F1 | Extractor | F1 | P | R | |---|--:|--:|--:| | **This fork (0177)** | **0.8633** | 0.8051 | 0.9305 | | resiliparse (upstream) | 0.8309 | 0.7693 | 0.9033 | | trafilatura (upstream) | 0.8073 | 0.8459 | 0.7721 | | Dripper | 0.7482 | 0.7328 | 0.7643 | ### Zyte article-extraction-benchmark — 181 docs, token-F1 | Extractor | F1 | P | R | |---|--:|--:|--:| | trafilatura (upstream) | **0.9520** | 0.9278 | 0.9775 | | Dripper | 0.9461 | 0.9073 | 0.9884 | | **This fork (0177)** | 0.8899 | 0.8106 | **0.9864** | | resiliparse (upstream) | 0.8806 | 0.7997 | 0.9799 | | marin v1.1 | 0.7766 | 0.7169 | 0.8471 | ### trafilatura eval set — 960 docs, containment F1 | Extractor | F1 | P | R | Acc | |---|--:|--:|--:|--:| | Dripper | **0.9335** | 0.9166 | 0.9511 | 0.9325 | | trafilatura (upstream) | 0.9130 | 0.9119 | 0.9141 | 0.9132 | | **This fork (0177)** | 0.8421 | 0.7656 | 0.9354 | 0.8251 | | resiliparse (upstream) | 0.8104 | 0.7142 | 0.9365 | 0.7816 | | marin v1.1 | 0.2353 | 0.8801 | 0.1358 | 0.5601 | ### Extraction unit tests — 100 tests | Extractor | Passed | |---|--:| | **This fork (0177)** | **97** | | resiliparse (upstream) | 90 | ours: code 13/13 · math 10/10 · tables 7/7 · attribution 12/12 · structure 5/5 ## WebMainBench fine-grained (en/dev, n=200, use_llm=false) | Extractor | overall | text | code | formula | table | TEDS | |---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:| | **This fork (0177)** | **0.6150** | **0.7951** | **0.8229** | **0.3673** | 0.4143 | **0.6756** | | Dripper | 0.5852 | 0.7174 | 0.7647 | 0.2488 | **0.5343** | 0.6609 | | mdx-v5think | 0.5115 | 0.7405 | 0.5908 | 0.3522 | 0.3294 | 0.5447 | | mdx-v12 | 0.4997 | 0.7614 | 0.4845 | 0.3441 | 0.3577 | 0.5508 | | mdx-d5+guards | 0.4989 | 0.7547 | 0.4909 | 0.3497 | 0.3487 | 0.5504 | | trafilatura | 0.3558 | 0.7733 | 0.1609 | 0.3508 | 0.1828 | 0.3113 | | extract_head | 0.2948 | 0.7836 | 0.0891 | 0.3069 | 0.1245 | 0.1699 | | upstream resiliparse | 0.2352 | 0.7561 | 0.0562 | 0.3635 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | Denominators: text 200 · code 42 · table 41 · formula 126. Formula on the 115 annotated-equation docs: ours 0.3838 · Dripper 0.1579.
**CLASSIFIER CASCADE** Had Claude try a bunch more architectures: Seems like **ettin68** from this [JHU paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.11412) training optimal encoders and decoders is nearly as good as modernBERT but twice as fast. Also using Rav's pooled tranformer shallow architecture is 172x as fast as modernBERT but only slightly worse. **WITH THIS I HAVE THE FOLLOWING SETTINGS**: One version that is currently running: Coverage looks promising: http://localhost:8096/#coverage Will get me the **10k WARCs later today and I will immediately start mixing** to compare with **DCLM**, **High_Quality**, and **Resiliparse** (running now) Another promising version: Half the time, but similar performance. **CURRENT BRANCHES I AM STILL EXPLORING** - Running filtering AFTER extraction since our new resiliparse-rust version is so fast - 10x the data on Rav's pooled transformer architecture since it is also much faster to train. So modernBERT takes 5 days to train on 10M docs, but we can train this on ~100M docs in similar time.
**TAKEAWAY** > [!TIP] > Our exploration of different architectures to distill the pipeline into has yielded a really fast and really quality pipeline. I am still exploring a few more knobs to tweak but we are getting ~0.85 F1 on filtering decisions and ~0.8 Levenstein similarity to LLM based spec-driven curation. ---
10k WARC Extraction Status LLM Pipeline v1.1 has 1 week to go if we decide this is the best use of cluster time:
**TAKEAWAY** > [!TIP] > We need one more week to extract LLM Pipeline v1.1 if we choose to use the cluster time for that. ---
Planning **RISKS** 1. **Maybe you really shouldn't get too much data and then mix it**. We are getting mixed results from **high_quality** vs **dclm**, however this is only mildly concerning because **high_quality** was never meant to be the "super high-coverage data source". **llm_pipeline_v1.1** is supposed to be this so if we can't mix it we are in trouble. === **DERISK:** Don't wait on the 10k extraction, get that mixing later today on the distilled version!! 2. **Everything looks great at sub 10^22 flops, but once we scale up...**. I think we need to test things at real scale SOON. This was out of the question for llm extraction, but I think it is feasible with our distilled pipeline now. **DERISK:** It might be time to train with no epoching, something like 3B models for 200B tokens or similar so we can trust benchmarks like DCLM Core. 3. **There is no distinction between good data and good data for human-centered applications**. I don't believe this, but **dclm** was beating us on blend. **DERISK:** I think we need more human-centered benchmarks. **NICE TO HAVE** - Safety pretraining style rewrites. **MUST HAVE** - High quality copywrite filtering to remove copywritten content from common crawl. With both of these we know that 3k WARC files is enough to get decent distillation from an llm filter. We could consider even training these as fastText classifiers or text rules (in the case of copywrite) - though safety might be more advanced, and run this once we are already starting to process the dataset. I presented this plan to Diyi and Will (separately). Diyi liked it but Will was more inclined to say this should all be one thing: **NEXT STEPS:** - [ ] Run training and evals on the new data from the distilled pipeline at 10k WARCs - [ ] Compare with resiliparse - [ ] Finish architecture sweeps for the distilled pipeline - [ ] Launch more data extraction on the distilled pipeline so we can test things at scale - [ ] Add more human centered benchmarks besides BLEnD
